briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Repeal Momentum Builds in Lansing as DEA and FDA Accelerate Federal Cannabis-Psychedelics Reform
briefs.top: Michigan's 24% wholesale tax fight has jumped into the governor's race, with GOP nominee John James pulling in industry cash on a repeal pledge — even as new stores keep opening and operators find workarounds. Nationally, the DEA's rescheduling hearing wrapped in July and FDA is now fast-tracking psychedelic therapies, with Compass Pathways on track for a Q4 NDA filing.

local.text: GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is courting Michigan cannabis industry donors with a pledge to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax, netting nearly $90,000 from a single JARS Cannabis-hosted fundraiser — a sign operators now have real electoral leverage heading into November.

Lawmakers from both parties have now backed repeal proposals including House Bill 6224, arguing the tax has generated far less revenue than projected while piling pressure on licensed operators — bipartisan cover that improves the odds of relief.

Jars Cannabis negotiated the removal of a police-monitored Flock surveillance camera at its Madison Heights store after a public standoff, a win for operator pushback against invasive local enforcement conditions.

Fields Cannary, a hospitality-forward dispensary-and-restaurant concept in Muskegon, is targeting a fall opening — a format bet that pushes Michigan retail further than most stores in the state have gone, even amid the tax squeeze.

The wholesale tax is badly underperforming forecasts — about $37 million in Q2 2026 and $34 million in Q1 against an initial estimate of $105 million per quarter — evidence operators can use to press lawmakers for a rate cut or repeal.

national.text: FDA finalized its clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA and will hold a public hearing September 14 on therapeutic use of psychedelics, building the regulatory infrastructure for what could soon be a live approval docket.

Compass Pathways is on track for a Q4 2026 NDA submission for its psilocybin therapy COMP360 after the drug showed six-month durability in treatment-resistant depression, with a possible launch in the first half of 2027.

FDA issued Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers to Compass Pathways, Usona Institute and Transcend Therapeutics, compressing standard drug review from roughly ten months to as little as one to two months for their psilocybin and methylone programs.

Curaleaf's bid for Canadian operator Aurora signals the improving capital backdrop from partial federal rescheduling is now opening the door to cross-border MSO consolidation — a template other major operators are watching closely.

The House hemp THC recriminalization deadline has been pushed back to December 11 under a bill President Trump signed, giving hemp-derived product makers and retailers more runway before facing federal contraband status.
